subject.title: fix(agents): prevent recursive task execution during model fallback

question: Should this PR land as an explicitly scoped embedded `sessions_spawn` mitigation while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92271 tracks remaining delegation surfaces, or should it wait for one shared work-spawning policy seam?
rationale: The patch changes fallback-turn delegation policy and intentionally leaves related gateway, inter-session send, cron, and Codex-native spawn surfaces uncovered, so automation cannot choose the permanent fail-closed boundary or cross-repo ownership.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
options.body: Merge the embedded `sessions_spawn` guard with the canonical issue left open for gateway, `sessions_send`/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups.

options.title: Harden Completion Text First
options.body: Before merge, extend the evidence-not-directive guard to the generic agent-harness completion path or narrow the PR claims to subagent announcements only.

options.title: Pause For Shared Seam
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers choose a common work-spawning policy seam that can cover OpenClaw tools and Codex-native delegation consistently.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
recommendation.body: Merge the embedded `sessions_spawn` guard with the canonical issue left open for gateway, `sessions_send`/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned and authored the cross-harness review that defined the unresolved scope question.
